target_profile.system_boundary: Captured HashiCorp Raft Go module: consensus loops, replication, membership, log/snapshot interfaces and FSM completion. FSM application semantics and durable backend implementation are caller-selected; in-repository mechanisms remain in scope.
ownership: Main loop owns normal protocol/configuration processing; replication, FSM and snapshot routines have distinct asynchronous duties.
NetworkTransport can invoke restricted zero-data heartbeat callbacks independently.
selection_injection: NewRaft accepts stores, FSM and Transport; network and in-memory transports are provided in repository.
unknowns: Backend-specific crash atomicity and alternate transport ordering remain outside this initial reading.

facts.meaning: The main loop has selected this node as leader after the campaign grant count reaches its configured voter majority.
facts.validity_context: Active leadership tenure; state can change through newer term, lease failure, removal, transfer-related RPC or shutdown.
facts.durability: Term and vote are persisted; Leader state is volatile.
facts.recovery: Startup becomes follower and campaigns again.

facts.meaning: A captured leader commitment object records a monotonically increasing stored-prefix match for a configured voter ID.
facts.validity_context: Only voter IDs present in that commitment map are accepted; configuration update retains matches for retained voter IDs.
facts.durability: Volatile; local logs and remote acknowledged storage are its inputs.
facts.recovery: Fresh leadership starts all matches at zero; snapshot/log acknowledgments rebuild support.

facts.meaning: The local Raft commitIndex is the index through which processLogs is authorized by the current handler to enqueue local entries; this is not itself proof of FSM completion or leader/follower content agreement.
facts.validity_context: Leader updates from tenure commitment; follower updates from leader-advertised index bounded by local last index after request checks.
facts.durability: Volatile commit accounting; persisted logs and snapshots preserve history.
facts.recovery: Startup restores applied snapshot boundary and reconstructs configuration; later leader commitment or AppendEntries reestablishes commit advancement.

facts.meaning: A verifyFuture contains its initial self vote plus positive per-peer notifications received while its notifyCh remains active; the threshold is the latest voter majority computed when verification begins.
facts.validity_context: Registered during an active leader tenure; peers are selected from replState, without a suffrage filter at registration or notification.
facts.recovery: No recovery; leader exit fails pending requests and new invocation allocates a fresh future.

facts.meaning: The stable store contains a LastVoteTerm integer and LastVoteCand byte string, read together by the vote handler as its prior-vote record; the two keys are written separately and do not intrinsically assert completion of the same persistVote call.
facts.validity_context: Values most recently retained by separate successful writes, including a prefix of an errored persistVote attempt.
facts.durability: StableStore persists each successful write; the interface exposes no multi-key transaction.
facts.recovery: NewRaft restores currentTerm; requestVote reads these keys directly when processing later requests, including after restart.
unknowns: Which concrete durable backends expose the scoped fail-without-overwrite candidate write?

surfaces.reason: Can normal backtracking or a legal overlap ever deliver a batch ending before a divergent local suffix while advertising a greater commit index?
Verification threshold counts voters but notification registration spans all replication peers. Determine applicable support responsibility and legal consequence.
A successful vote-term write followed by a candidate-key error can retain an older candidate; determine the applicable freshness duty and actual producer history for the duplicate grant.
Fast path excludes log/commit data but changes term/state concurrently with normal processing; overlapping ownership merits separate examination.

formation.explanation: A1: leader dispatch assigns term/index and persists logs before recording its match and notifying peer replicators. Per-peer requests carry previous prefix, bounded entries and commit index; success supplies stored-prefix support to a captured commitment object. Only configured voters count, and its majority index must reach the first entry of this leader term. The main loop consumes commit notification, marks configuration committed and queues logs. Followers validate term/previous prefix, truncate supplied conflicts and propagate leader commit accounting into their own queue. FSM execution and future completion occur later on the FSM goroutine. Snapshot transfer substitutes a persisted/restored prefix when logs are unavailable.

context.explanation: A2: contact timeout triggers a eligible local voter campaign; pre-vote probes where supported, then electSelf persists a new term/self vote and asks configured voters through a campaign-local response channel. Vote receivers reject ineligible/stale or less-up-to-date candidates and preserve one vote per term. Majority grants install leader state. Higher-term requests, replication higher-term responses, loss of lease quorum and committed removal can end tenure. Transfer first catches up its target then requests an accelerated campaign. Startup restores term, snapshot and membership history but starts as follower.

connection.explanation: Each tenure creates fresh commitment/replication objects, captures its term and sends a no-op; the current-term threshold constrains commitment of inherited history. Old RPC replies retain old campaign channels or commitment pointers, while follower term checks reject obsolete requests. Leader exit signals replication to stop and fails pending client/verify futures; it does not erase stored or already queued history. New authority is constrained by log freshness and recovered configuration. Configuration changes serialize after a current-term commit, then alter voter eligibility while retaining matching support for retained voters. Committed entries are separately consumed by the FSM, and a failed client future does not imply absence from later history. VerifyLeader is another authority consumer whose voter threshold and all-peer notifications have an unresolved eligibility relationship.

open_details: Nonvoter responses contribute to verification support under the existing all-peer notification mechanism; externally stale-read consequences under autonomous lease/election timing remain open.
Follower commit bound reachability under backtracking and overlapping work.
Partial stable-store failures; retained snapshot suffixes; heartbeat/main-loop context overlap; transfer cancellation races.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority transitions, old-work ownership, persistent recovery and application completion have been traced. Local anomalies and deeper variants remain open; usability is a basis for investigation, not a correctness or coverage claim.
